2 3 # Click 4 5 Click is a Python package for creating beautiful command line interfaces 6 in a composable way with as little code as necessary. It's the "Command 7 Line Interface Creation Kit". It's highly configurable but comes with 8 sensible defaults out of the box. 9 10 It aims to make the process of writing command line tools quick and fun 11 while also preventing any frustration caused by the inability to 12 implement an intended CLI API. 13 14 Click in three points: 15 16 - Arbitrary nesting of commands 17 - Automatic help page generation 18 - Supports lazy loading of subcommands at runtime 19 20 21 ## A Simple Example 22 23 ```python 24 import click 25 26 @click.command() 27 @click.option("--count", default=1, help="Number of greetings.") 28 @click.option("--name", prompt="Your name", help="The person to greet.") 29 def hello(count, name): 30 """Simple program that greets NAME for a total of COUNT times.""" 31 for _ in range(count): 32 click.echo(f"Hello, {name}!") 33 34 if __name__ == '__main__': 35 hello() 36 ``` 37 38 ``` 39 $ python hello.py --count=3 40 Your name: Click 41 Hello, Click! 42 Hello, Click! 43 Hello, Click! 44 ``` 45 46 47 ## Donate 48 49 The Pallets organization develops and supports Click and other popular 50 packages. In order to grow the community of contributors and users, and 51 allow the maintainers to devote more time to the projects, [please 52 donate today][]. 53 54 [please donate today]: https://palletsprojects.com/donate 55 56 ## Contributing 57 58 See our [detailed contributing documentation][contrib] for many ways to 59 contribute, including reporting issues, requesting features, asking or answering 60 questions, and making PRs. 61 62 [contrib]: https://palletsprojects.com/contributing/ 63

input.purpose: Click is a BSD-3-Clause Python library for building composable command-line interfaces. It provides decorators and classes (Command, Group, Option, Argument) that parse argv, convert values through typed ParamType objects, dispatch to nested subcommands, render help, provide shell tab-completion, and offer terminal utilities (prompts, styled echo, progress bars, pagers) and a CliRunner for testing. The repo declares version 8.5.1 (pyproject.toml L3) and CHANGES.md L1-3 dates that release 2026-11-09.
input.intended_users: Python developers writing command-line tools and scripts who want a decorator-based, composable CLI framework. Its tests and docs also serve maintainers and contributors (CONTRIBUTING via README L56-62, and the docs and typing tox envs in pyproject.toml).
languages: Python type annotations (typed package; mypy strict and pyright configured, pyproject.toml L107-117)
frameworks: Sphinx with myst-parser and pallets-sphinx-themes for docs (pyproject.toml L31-37)
tox with tox-uv for multi-env runs (pyproject.toml L145-232)
ruff for lint and format (pyproject.toml L119-143)
dependencies: No runtime dependencies declared in [project] (pyproject.toml L1-23 shows none). Only build-system and dev/test/docs/typing dependency groups (pyproject.toml L25-60).
Dev/test groups: ruff, tox, tox-uv, pytest, pytest-randomly, pytest-xdist, mypy, pyright, pre-commit, sphinx stack. Lock file: uv.lock (present, not read).

entry_points.description: Public package API. Re-exports Command, Group, Option, Argument, Context, decorators (command, group, option, argument, pass_context, ...), exceptions, types (INT, Choice, Path, File, ...) and termui helpers (echo, prompt, confirm, progressbar, style, ...). Lazily warns on deprecated names via module __getattr__ (L76-144).

Command.main(): the standard script entry point. Reads sys.argv (with Windows glob expansion), handles shell completion, builds the Context, invokes the command, and maps exceptions to exit codes (Command.main L1483-1617).
Command._main_shell_completion(): checks the _<PROG>_COMPLETE environment variable and delegates to shell_completion.shell_complete, then exits (L1619-1649).
@click.command decorator: wraps a function into a Command, attaching options and arguments declared with @option and @argument (decorators.py L168-262; @argument L324, @option L352).
@click.group decorator: same as command but creates a Group (multi-command container) (decorators.py L293-313).
CliRunner: in-process invocation for tests, with output and stdin capture (CliRunner L317-351, invoke L595).

key_modules.role: Core object model. Context (L213) holds per-invocation state and invoke/fail/exit. Command (L960) has make_context, parse_args, invoke, and main. Group (L1671) adds subcommand resolution, chaining, and invoke_without_command. Parameter (L2209) with Option (L2891) and Argument (L3698) handles value sourcing (consume_value L2518), type conversion (type_cast_value L2566), defaults and envvars (process_value L2640), and parse-result handling (handle_parse_result L2763). ParameterSource enum (L174).

Internal option parser modelled on optparse (_OptionParser L224). Tokenizes argv into option values, positional arguments, and an ordering list. It is wrapped by Command.make_parser and Command.parse_args. Deprecated as a public API (L237-238).

Parameter type system. ParamType base (L65) with convert/fail. Concrete types: StringParamType (L304), Choice (L342), DateTime (L522), IntParamType/IntRange (L736/744), FloatParamType/FloatRange (L768/776), BoolParamType (L819), UUIDParameterType (L888), File (L915), Path (L1059), Tuple (L1258). convert_type (L1356) maps Python defaults to types.

Decorator-based API that builds Command, Group, Option, and Argument, plus helpers such as pass_context, pass_obj, make_pass_decorator, version_option, help_option, confirmation_option, and password_option.

Shell tab-completion. shell_complete (L19) dispatches on the env var instruction (source or complete). ShellComplete base class (L277) with Bash (L388), Zsh (L447), Fish (L479), and PowerShell (L516) subclasses. CompletionItem (L67). add_completion_class and get_completion_class (L560/588) form a registry.
Help-text layout. HelpFormatter (L110) writes usage, sections, and definition lists with indentation and width, plus wrap_text (L31) and measure_table (L14).

Exception hierarchy used for user-facing errors and exit codes. ClickException (L35) is the base, with UsageError (L68), BadParameter (L114), MissingParameter (L159), NoSuchOption (L232), NoSuchCommand (L268), FileError (L342). Abort (L362) and Exit (L366) are control-flow signals.

Interactive terminal utilities: prompt (L139/168), confirm (L289), progressbar (L403-443), style and secho (L641/780), edit (L815), launch (L923), getchar (L957), pause (L993), echo_via_pager (L367). Platform implementations live in _termui_impl.py and _winconsole.py.

Misc helpers: echo (L240), open_file (L381), format_filename (L430), get_app_dir (L472), _LazyFile (L103), _detect_program_name (L550), _expand_args (L605, Windows glob expansion used by Command.main).
Thread-local current-context stack. get_current_context (L20), push_context (L44), pop_context (L49), resolve_color_default (L54).
Test harness. CliRunner (L317) isolates stdin/stdout/env and invokes a command in-process. Result (L231) wraps output, exit_code, and exception. Capture modes are 'sys' or 'fd' (docstring L331-338).

Private, platform-specific and compatibility helpers. _winconsole handles Windows console I/O; _termui_impl holds ProgressBar (L44) and pager/edit internals; _compat handles stream and atomic-file details.
public_interfaces: private (underscore-prefixed); not part of the public API

input.execution_flow: 1) A script's console entry calls cli() which is Command.__call__ -> Command.main (core.py L1483, L1651). 2) main resolves args (sys.argv[1:], Windows-expanded at L1534-1540) and prog_name (L1542-1543). 3) _main_shell_completion (L1546, L1619-1649) checks _PROG_COMPLETE; if set it calls shell_completion.shell_complete and exits. 4) main calls self.make_context(prog_name, args) (L1559). make_context (L1330-1365) builds a Context (context_class) and calls parse_args inside ctx.scope(). 5) Command.parse_args (L1367-1398) creates a parser via make_parser (L1227), gets opts, leftover args, and order from _OptionParser.parse_args (parser.py L298-314), then calls param.handle_parse_result for each parameter in processing order (iter_params_for_processing, core.py L147). 6) handle_parse_result (L2763) calls consume_value (L2518: CLI value, then envvar, then default_map, then default) and process_value (L2640), which runs type_cast_value (L2566) and the ParamType.convert (types.py L65). Leftover args are stored in ctx.args. 7) main calls self.invoke(ctx) (L1560). For a plain Command, invoke (L1400-1414) calls ctx.invoke(callback, **ctx.params). For a Group (core.py L2020-2086), it resolves the subcommand with resolve_command (L2088-2112), which uses get_command/list_commands, then creates the sub-context with cmd.make_context(parent=ctx) and invokes it. In chain mode it creates all subcontexts first and invokes them in order. 8) Exceptions are caught in main (L1571-1617): Exit gives an exit code, Abort and KeyboardInterrupt print 'Aborted', ClickException shows its message and exit code (exceptions.py L35). The process then ends with sys.exit (L1612). With standalone_mode=False, main returns the value or re-raises instead. For tests, CliRunner.invoke (testing.py L595) runs main with standalone_mode and captures output into Result."}]

text: An Option resolves its default in `Parameter.consume_value`, which is the last fallback after the command line, environment variable, and default_map (`src/click/core.py` L2558-2562, calling `self.get_default(ctx)`). `Option.get_default` (`src/click/core.py` L3222-3246) is overridden to resolve auto-derived defaults lazily via `_resolve_lazy_default`. `Option.consume_value` (`src/click/core.py` L3627-3652) wraps the base call to handle flag sentinels and prompts. The default-value tests are in `tests/test_defaults.py`, which has cases such as `test_basic_defaults` (L22), `test_flag_default_map` (L110), and `test_default_map_source` (L253). I did not open these test bodies, so I have not confirmed which of them exercise `Option.get_default` specifically. Some default-related tests also live in `tests/test_basic.py` (e.g. `test_datetime_option_default`, L683).
